table.label: Table 42-1
table.title: The buttons of the controller
head: Button
What it does
rows: Left click: it opens, takes and presses.
Right click: it opens the context menu.
Back: it closes or backs out.
Tap: open, hide or show both windows. Hold: close both.
In a window, moves from control to control. With no window open, hold a direction for a wheel: *Character*, *World*, *Social* or *Here and now*.
Walk. In a window, click it to sort the list.
Aim; both windows hide. In a window, click it for *List* or *Grid*. In a wheel, point.
The *Character* window. No window open: LB + RB zooms out. Quick actions: LB + a button.
The *World* window. No window open: RB + LB zooms in. Quick actions: RB + a button.
The game's own: aim and attack. On the map, zoom.
In a window: layout. No window open: hold for the ZeD wheel.

blocks.p: Every mouse action has a button: *A* is the left click, *X* is the right click and *B* backs out. Figure 42-1 shows where each button is, and Table 42-1 says what it does.
Choose the button pictures in *ZeD setup*, under *Controls*.

marks.text: LT | RT: the game's own, aim and attack. On the map, zoom.
LB: Character window. Quick actions: LB + a button.
RB: World window. Quick actions: RB + a button.
Y: tap to open, hide or show both windows. Hold: close both.
B: back. Close or back out.
A: left click. Open, take, press.
X: right click, the context menu.

sticky.text: Every mouse action has a button.
